newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:
Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the Commission had just decided to ban the use of the drug avoparcin in animal feed.
He said the informal Transport Council this weekend would discuss negotiations with Switzerland, interoperability of road pricing systems and air traffic management and safety.

Responding to questions about the visit of Gibraltar's chief minister Peter Caruna, spokesman Peter Guilford said Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan had reminded him that EU membership entailed both rights and obligations, including implementation of EU financial services directives. Spokeswoman Betty Olivi said the Commission was working with Gibraltar to set dates and objectives for improving its record in implementing EU legislation.
She said the Commission was studying complaints by Gibraltar that Britain and Spain had taken measures against it that violated the EU treaty.
Vale de Almeida said he had no reaction from Commission President Jacques Santer on comments by a Toyota official that Britain could lose investment if if failed to join the single currency.
In response to a question, Vale de Almeida said the EU would have to come up with a new assessment if Turkey submitted a new EU membership application, but any other speculation was premature.

Asked about French resistance to proposals for a new approach to EU anti-dumping policy, Guilford said the subject was being debated internally and meetings were taking place on the subject on Thursday with the Dutch presidency in The Hague.
Responding to charges that the Commission's staff was not ethnically diverse, Vale de Almeida said Santer had described the European project as anti-racist in nature.

Vale de Almeida said the Commission would not comment on possible plans by the European Parliament to censure the Commission as a result of its BSE inquiry until the parliament had finalised its report. He said the Commission was "serene" about the issue.
Guilford said he would take questions later in the day on the visit of Thai Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee and Hong Kong Democratic Party Chairman Martin Lee.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/71: Ban on the antibiotic "Avoparcin" in animal feed.
- IP/97/72: European Year against Racism is launched in the Hague.
- IP/97/73: The Employment and Labour Market Committee holds its first meeting.
- IP/97/74: Emma Bonino on mission in Zaire.
- Speech/97/22: Speech by Commission President Jacques Santer at the conference opening the European Year against Racism.
